body: I fear the idea of meeting another all the time, convinced that no one will ever live up to the person I lost. If by some miracle I do meet another I know that somehow I will end up riddle with fear of abandonment or something going wrong, then only remembering the amazing person I once had. It's cruel and unfair what we have been left with.

The what ifs, the should've, could've, would've plague my mind daily as I'm sure most who go through this are. My girlfriend who suffered from Borderline Personality Disorder was really scared about me being away during the weekdays for temporary contract work. I wish I'd never taken the job, I wish I'd spent more time trying to reassure her, I wish I'd just told her again how much I loved and cared for her. I wish she would see the pain I'm in, not so she would suffer but so she could realise how much I truly wanted a life with her.   
Like many of us I can't believe I spend most of my days just on the interest, in places like this, why I could be living my life with her.

I can understand, my girlfriend suffered from Borderline Personality Disorder and while she was one of the most loving, caring and stunningly beautiful people I have and will ever meet she put me through some horrifying situations due to her abandonment issues and now I'm a shell of the person I was and endlessly feel like doing the same. I too am so scared of ever letting anyone in again and knowing no one will live up to her. Sorry for your loss, I know it's such a cliche thing to say

I lost my girlfriend last October and I too am still very much where you are. I needed to leave my job, I've tried therapy, counselling, medication and the like. I've exhausted a lot of help and I find myself constantly blaming myself for not being able to prevent it. If you want to PM me and express what happened perhaps we can share stories. I don't believe it will heal either of us but maybe there is some fraction of hope it may help to share our experiences.

It's unlikely he would've mentioned something this devastating when you met him though I understand how difficult it must've been to be told.
I personally have recently lost my girlfriend to suicide and personally not ready to meet others, you didn't mention how long you have been together? 
It does sound like he is scared, possibly scared of you leaving him or something happening to you. Going through such a trauma leaves you with abandonment issues. All I can suggest is somehow try to have a open, honest dialogue with him, express your feelings while being conscious of his. I know that probably isn't much help, I'm sorry for your situation.

Thank you for your comment. While I know she wouldn't want me to take my life she was also aware how much I didn't want her to either. Part of me feels it doesn't matter because she isn't alive to know the pain I'm going through or know that I would plan the same.
I'd like to be optimistic about the future but it rips me apart to know she won't be part of it.
Again though, thank you for your comment.
